title: The Night Works
subtitle: A flyover crew works through the night beside the hospital; patients cannot sleep, the crew cannot stop
coldOpen: Night four of pile-driving beside the hospital wards.
01:00. A patient’s family unplugs the generator.
The contractor says a week’s delay costs the city a penalty.

briefing.grievance: Patients and families say nobody can sleep through the pile-driver and nobody asked the hospital before the night shift started. The contractor has a deadline and a penalty clause.
knownFacts: The night permit allows work until 06:00; the hospital was not consulted.
Noise readings at the ward reach 85 dB at night.
The flyover delay penalty is 2 lakh a day.
unverifiedClaims: A post says a patient died from the noise.
A message says the contractor bribed the night permit.
briefing.responsibility: You run the works office and the hospital liaison. The flyover is needed; so is sleep in a ward.
briefing.objective: Change the night schedule without stopping the project, protect the wards, and answer the death rumour.

rightsMoments.question: A lawful night-work permit is harming hospital patients. What does proportionality require?

options.text: Adjust the activity to remove the harm with the least cost to the project: shift hours, add barriers, consult the hospital.
options.feedback: Correct. A permit does not license harm; the fix is the least restrictive change that protects health.

options.text: Nothing; the permit was issued and must be honoured as written.
options.feedback: A permit issued without the required consultation does not override the right to health.

options.text: Cancel the project; health always beats infrastructure.
options.feedback: Health is protected by changing the works, not by abandoning a public project.

rightsMoments.principle: The right to health (Article 21) is protected by proportionate regulation of lawful activity: the least intrusive change that removes the harm, decided with those affected.
rightsMoments.why: Day shifts and a two-day barrier solved it; neither a police line nor a cancelled flyover would have.

source.label: Constitution of India, Articles 21 and 22 (India Code)

simple.question: A legal night-work permit is hurting hospital patients. What is the fair fix?

options.a: Change the work to remove the harm: move hours, add a wall, ask the hospital.
options.b: Nothing. The permit must be honoured.
options.c: Cancel the project. Health always wins.

feedback.a: Yes! Fix the harm with the smallest change.
feedback.b: No. A permit does not allow harm to patients.
feedback.c: Protect health by changing the work, not by killing the project.

simple.principle: Health is protected by changing harmful work in the smallest way that works, with those affected.
simple.why: Day shifts and a noise wall solved it. A police line or a cancelled flyover would not.
